chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) underwent cupping, and the freed slave of Banu Bayadah performed it for him. He gave him the payment (for the service), and if it were forbidden, he would not have given it to him. When he finished, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Where is the blood?' He said, 'I drank it, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'It was not fitting for you to do that, for Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has made it a barrier for you from the Fire, so do not repeat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking blood from cupping in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the permissibility of consuming blood in specific medicinal contexts, as evidenced by the Prophet’s affirmation that it serves as a 'barrier from Hellfire' for the cupper. While the Prophet instructed the practitioner not to repeat the act, Shia scholars often interpret this as a recommendation (*istihbab*) or a specific circumstance rather than a prohibition, distinguishing it from the general prohibition of blood in dietary laws. The narrative underscores the practical wisdom of cupping in Islamic medicine and the spiritual merit attached to its proper execution.
